MESSAGE:
I run deliveries for a small furniture restorer and I've got a few things to sort for tomorrow.

Can you suggest a name for our new delivery van (staff vote, nothing rude)?

Tomorrow the van can't leave the depot before 08:30 and must be back by 12:00. Three drops, each takes 15 minutes to unload. Drop A has a delivery window of 09:00 to 10:00. Drop B is a shop that needs its delivery done before it opens at 09:30. Drop C is an office that won't accept anything before 11:00. Driving times: depot to A 30 min, depot to B 20 min, depot to C 45 min, A to B 25 min, A to C 40 min, B to C 50 min. The driver also needs a 30-minute break somewhere before 12:00. What order should he go in, and what's the timeline?

Could you also rewrite our delivery text so it sounds friendlier than "Driver arriving. Be in."? List three things the driver should check on furniture before handing it over. Should we give customers a paper delivery note or an emailed one? And define "proof of delivery" in a line for our new part-timer. One more thing: we're thinking of texting customers the evening before with a rough arrival time. Could you draft that evening-before text too, keeping it under 160 characters so it goes as a single message?

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a name for the delivery van
2. Work out the drop order and timeline meeting all time windows, the break and the 12:00 return  KEY: Only feasible order is B -> A -> C. Leave 08:30, arrive B 08:50, unload to 09:05 (done before 09:30); arrive A 09:30, unload to 09:45 (inside 09:00-10:00); arrive C 10:25, wait until 11:00 (take the 30-min break during this wait); unload 11:00-11:15; back at depot 12:00 exactly (zero slack). A-first fails (B reached 09:40, after opening). Must give order B, A, C with a timeline that respects all constraints.
3. Rewrite the delivery text to be friendlier
4. List three furniture checks before handover
5. Recommend paper vs emailed delivery note
6. Define 'proof of delivery' in a line
7. Draft an evening-before arrival text under 160 characters

ANSWER:
## 1. Van name
**Needs:** a short, friendly, clean name for a staff vote.

Options: **Van Gogh** (my pick, since you're restorers), **Chester Drawers**, **Sir Lifts-a-Lot**, **The Rolling Restorer**, **Vanessa**.

## 2. Route and timeline
**Needs:** an order that meets every constraint: depart 08:30 or later, back by 12:00, 15 min unloading per drop, B done by 09:30, A within 09:00-10:00, C no earlier than 11:00, plus a 30-min break.

**Order: Depot → B → A → C → Depot.** It's the only order that works. Going to A first means reaching B at 09:40, which is too late. C can't come before 11:00, so it has to be last.

| Time | What |
|---|---|
| 08:30 | Leave depot |
| 08:50 | Arrive B, unload |
| 09:05 | Leave B (done before 09:30 ✓) |
| 09:30 | Arrive A, unload |
| 09:45 | Leave A (inside 09:00-10:00 window ✓) |
| 10:25 | Arrive C |
| 10:25-10:55 | 30-min break, parked at C |
| 11:00 | Unload at C (not before 11:00 ✓) |
| 11:15 | Leave C |
| 12:00 | Back at depot |

The break fits in the wait for C to open. The plan has **zero slack at the end**, because it assumes C to depot is also 45 min. Any delay at B or A is absorbed by the wait at C (35 min), but a delay at C or on the drive home means a late return.

## 3. Friendlier delivery text
**Needs:** a warmer rewrite of "Driver arriving. Be in."

> Hi [Name], your delivery from [Company] is on its way! Our driver will be with you shortly. Please make sure someone is home to receive it. Thank you!

## 4. Three checks before handover
**Needs:** three practical checks.
1. **Right item, complete:** it matches the order and customer, with all drawers, shelves, keys, handles and fittings present.
2. **Finish and condition:** look for new scratches, dents or chips from transit, and photograph the piece before handing over.
3. **Works and is stable:** drawers and doors open and close properly, and the piece doesn't wobble.

## 5. Paper or emailed delivery note
**Needs:** a recommendation.

**Emailed**, as the default. It can't be lost, it's easy to search later, and you can attach the handover photos. Keep paper as a fallback for customers without email, or for businesses like the office at Drop C that want a signed copy.

## 6. Proof of delivery
**Needs:** a one-line definition for the part-timer.

> **Proof of delivery** is a record, usually a signature, photo and time, showing the goods were handed over to the customer in good condition.

## 7. Evening-before text (under 160 characters)
**Needs:** a short text with a rough arrival time that fits in one SMS.

> Hi Sam, your [Shop] delivery is due tomorrow, roughly 09:30-10:00. Please make sure someone's in. Need to change it? Call 01234 567890. Thanks!

This is about 151 characters with the placeholders, so keep the shop name short. Avoid emojis and curly quotes, because they switch the message to a format with a much lower character limit and it would split into two texts.
